panels.title: Plant weight — every weighing, at the time it happened
panels.description: Raw readings plotted where they actually fall in time, not bucketed into days. Weighing happens when someone is free, not on a schedule, and a pot also drifts through the day with the plant's own respiration — so a daily bucket imposed a grid the measurements do not have and hid both effects. A watering shows here as a step up, drying as the slope between steps.

panels.title: Water use rate (g/day) — normalised for the gap between weighings
panels.description: Weight lost per 24 hours, computed between consecutive weighings and divided by the actual elapsed time — so a 19-hour gap and a 3-day gap are directly comparable. Positive means the plant drank it. Pairs less than an hour apart are excluded: those are the same session, not an interval. ⚠ Still read with care — the changes are a few grams on pots of 130-2200 g, and the 2026-08-06 session appears to carry a systematic offset of about -6 g. Use mark-weight.sh to label a session suspect and it will drop out of every chart.

panels.title: Water added (g) — each watering, at the time it happened
panels.description: Every jump of more than 10 g between two consecutive weighings — one bar per watering, at the moment it was recorded, not one per day. Water twice in a day and you see two bars, which is the truth; the previous version kept only the largest jump per calendar day. Weighing before and after gives the exact amount; if only the post-water reading was taken, the pair becomes previous-weighing-to-post-water, which measures water added minus whatever the plant used in between.

panels.title: DLI per day (lux estimate)
panels.description: Daily light integral from the BH1750, lux/54. This is the figure the light controller tops up against (DLI_TARGET, default 4.0), so it is the one to read when asking whether the evening top-up did its job. Absolute scale is not trustworthy — lux/54 is a daylight conversion applied to an LED — so read it relatively.

targets.query:
import "timezone"
option location = timezone.location(name: "Asia/Taipei")

from(bucket: "sensors")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "air" and r._field == "lux" and r.device == "livingroom")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _value: r._value / 54.0 }))
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1d, fn: (tables=<-, column) => tables |> integral(unit: 1s), createEmpty: false)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _value: r._value / 1000000.0 }))
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> yield(name: "DLI lux est.")

panels.title: Outdoor solar & rain per day (板橋)
panels.description: Open-Meteo daily context. Indoor light barely tracks this — natural light measured at 1-2% of the indoor daily total on 2026-07-30 — so treat it as weather context, not as an explanation of indoor DLI.

targets.query:

from(bucket: "sensors")

  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1d, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> yield(name: "solar mean")

panels.title: Lamp — when it switched off each day
panels.description: Local hour of the last lamp-off. 18.5 = the base window end (18:30, no top-up); ~19.8-20.1 = the evening top-up ran and reached DLI_TARGET; 20.5 = it ran to the EXTEND_END cap without reaching target, i.e. the lamp delivered less light than usual that day. Restricted to 17:00-21:30 because light/state is retained and every Telegraf reconnect replays it as a phantom OFF.

panels.title: Ingest completeness — points per day
panels.description: Points stored per day per pipeline. This is the panel that makes a silent outage visible: the Open-Meteo 503 collapse shows here as weather dropping from ~96/day to 3-10/day between 2026-07-30 and 08-03, and the recovery back to 96 after the poll interval was cut to 5 min. A pipeline going flat is the signal — the absolute heights differ by design.

targets.query:
import "timezone"
option location = timezone.location(name: "Asia/Taipei")

base = from(bucket: "sensors") |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)

// One representative field per measurement — counting every field would mix
// value types in one group, which aggregateWindow rejects.
union(tables: [
  base |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "air" and r._field == "lux"),
  base |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "spectrum" and r._field == "f555"),
  base |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "weather" and r._field == "temperature_2m"),
  base |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "plant_weight" and r._field == "weight_g"),
])
  |> group(columns: ["_measurement"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1d, fn: count, createEmpty: true)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "_measurement"])
